title: Finite data and finite relations descend in a filtered colimit
statement:
Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set and $(A_i)_{i\in I}$ a directed system of commutative rings (ring maps $A_i\to A_j$ for $i\le j$, compatible) with colimit $A$ in the category of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Given
finitely many elements of $A$ and finitely many equalities between ring
expressions in those elements, there exists one stage $i$ and lifts of all
selected elements to $A_i$ for which all selected equalities hold. Once
they hold at $i$, they hold after every transition $A_i\to A_j$.

proof.text: Use the filtered-category instance of the nonempty directed preorder. For each selected element choose a representative by Concrete.colimit_exists_rep, the first clause of [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise]. Apply Mathlib Finset.exists_le to the finite image of the representative stages; move every representative along its transition to this common stage. Naturality of colimit.ι proves that these are still lifts of the selected elements.

For every polynomial equation, MvPolynomial.hom_eval₂ and RingHom.eq_intCast' show that its two evaluated representatives have equal images in the colimit. By Concrete.colimit_exists_of_rep_eq, the second clause of [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise], their images agree at a later stage. The two arrows from the common stage to that stage coincide because a preorder category has subsingleton hom sets.

Apply Mathlib Finset.exists_le to the finite set consisting of the common stage and all equality-witness stages. Map each witnessed equality to this upper bound. Functoriality and uniqueness of preorder morphisms identify the composite transitions, while MvPolynomial.hom_eval₂ and RingHom.eq_intCast' identify the mapped evaluations. This gives all equations simultaneously, and colimit naturality preserves the lifts. Applying any later ring homomorphism to an equation, using the same evaluation identities, proves its persistence.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $(A_i)_{i\in I}$ be a directed system of rings with colimit $A$. Given
finitely many elements of $A$ and finitely many equalities between ring
expressions in those elements, there exists one stage $i$ and lifts of all
selected elements to $A_i$ for which all selected equalities hold. Once
they hold at $i$, they hold after every transition $A_i\to A_j$.

proof.text:
Choose a representative stage for each selected element. Directedness and
[lemma-nagata-directed-finite-upper-bound] place all representatives at
one common stage. Equality of two representatives in a filtered colimit is
witnessed at a later stage. There are only finitely many equalities, so a
second finite upper bound makes them all true simultaneously. Ring
homomorphisms preserve the equalities at every later stage.
